text:
Matthew Schaefer is 19 and plays defense, and on Tuesday he scored three goals against Columbus. Daily Faceoff noted he became the third teenage NHL defenseman to record a hat trick. It was the Islanders' second straight game with a hat trick, after Simon Holmstrom's first career one in Anaheim, and their third straight win. Schaefer has 15 points in his last 10 games and a six-game point streak, and by our numbers it's earned: the chances are rising with the points.

The team around him is a harder read. The Islanders are plus-9 in goals on minus-9.1 expected (the quality of the chances), and the gap is almost all Ilya Sorokin, at 11.1 goals saved above expected this season and better than his save percentage looks against hard shots. That is a real skill, Sorokin has done it for years, but at five on five the Islanders hold 49% of the chances, and in the last five only 46%. Mathew Barzal is easing back after a knee problem he called the "hardest journey of my life," per the New York Post. Logan Stanley returns to Winnipeg for the first time after 261 games with the Jets.

Winnipeg just had a six-game winning streak snapped by Ottawa, 2-1, a game it got only 31% of the chances in. Before that the Jets were winning the chance battle almost every night, and Mark Scheifele became the franchise's career points leader with a four-point night in Chicago, where the Jets came back from four goals down for the second time this season, per Ken Wiebe of the Winnipeg Free Press. Dylan DeMelo is on injured reserve. Nino Niederreiter is one point from 500, Alex Iafallo one from 300, and Kyle Connor, already past 700 career points, leads our goal projections on either side at 48%. Stuart Skinner, at +1.1, is in net.

Our model has this close, 3.12 to 3.03 in expected goals for Winnipeg. Our sleeper is Cole Perfetti, 55% for a point on a line that creates 4.24 expected goals per 60.
headline: Schaefer brings his hat trick to Winnipeg
